function.mechanism: Conjugated polyene chromophore absorbs visible light (red/orange pigment), producing coloring effects in foods.

adi.basis: ADI of 0.5 mg/kg bw/day established in EFSA 2008 opinion and retained in 2017 extension-of-use evaluation; refined scenarios did not indicate concern, but conservative high-intake scenarios could exceed ADI in some groups.

efsa.key_finding: E160d remained acceptable under refined exposure assumptions; potential ADI exceedance in conservative high-exposure scenarios, especially children/toddlers.

adi.basis: Source-dependent records: tomato extract entry (2009) shows group ADI 'not specified'; Blakeslea trispora entry shows group ADI 0-0.5 mg/kg bw (2006, with 2023 specification-focused entry retaining this value).

concerns.summary: EFSA conservative exposure scenarios at proposed maximum use levels showed possible ADI exceedance in toddlers/children and some high-intake scenarios.
Source-dependent JECFA ADI entries (not specified vs 0-0.5 mg/kg bw) create interpretation complexity for mixed-source market use.

In a 2024 phase I oncology study, synthetic lycopene co-administered with docetaxel modestly increased docetaxel exposure; one dose-limiting toxicity was reported at the top tested lycopene dose in that treatment context.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2008 reported no concern for genotoxicity/carcinogenicity in the evaluated dossier context.
A 90-day rat study of lycopene from Blakeslea trispora found no observed toxicity up to the highest tested dose (NOEL at top dose).
No IARC group classification for lycopene was identified in the current IARC list-of-classifications dataset checked (updated 2026-02-25).

populations: some high-intake adults in conservative combined-source assumptions
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined scenarios indicated lower risk than conservative maximum-level scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory approvals and generally reassuring toxicology support use at regulated levels, but ADI exceedance is plausible in conservative child high-intake scenarios, which introduces a meaningful caveat.
key_factors: EFSA conservative exposure scenarios can exceed ADI in children/toddlers
FDA CFR approval under 21 CFR 73.585 with GMP and exemption-from-certification conditions
JECFA entries show source-dependent ADI framing
